sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A blueprint for products with no server and no database of yours.
sections.para: Phase one is a folder of HTML, CSS and JavaScript, native web components and vendored libraries, that runs offline and anywhere. The user brings the AI key, the storage and the passkey, so no request passes through you. The gaps are capped user keys and paying the app; then how to build, charge, and a checklist for agents.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight points: the architecture, the gaps, the team, the price, the checklist.
sections.para: No server or database of yours; native components, vendored, running anywhere; the user's key, storage and passkey; not in the line; the pieces mostly exist; build with agents and an explorer; charge for build, users and keys; a checklist for agents.

sections.label: What this is
sections.line: The pieces in one place, for founders and their agents, and a name.
sections.para: Many earlier articles are one idea in pieces: passkeys, your own key, less code, Cloudflare blocks, explorer coding, your own newsroom, pay after the value. This is the blueprint, written for founders and for the agents that work with them. Its name: a no-server product, as distinct from serverless.

sections.label: The principles
sections.line: Ten principles, from no server to charging for value.
sections.para: No server or database of yours; native web components; vendored libraries; offline and anywhere; the user brings the compute; the user's data stays with the user; the passkey is the identity; you are not in the line; version control and agents; charge for value, not servers.

sections.label: A worked example: an infographic studio
sections.line: An infographic studio, end to end, with nothing through the company.
sections.para: The user opens static files, signs in with a passkey, connects OpenRouter by OAuth so requests bill their own credit, generates in the browser and keeps the results in their storage or Drive app folder. A simulation mode lets every feature work without a key.

sections.label: The gaps today
sections.line: Where the providers fall short today, and the opportunity.
sections.para: No documented cap on a user-granted key; OpenAI and Google warn against developer keys in client code; Sign in with ChatGPT is a limited trial needing a backend; no provider checked pays the app that brings a customer; GitHub Pages is not for commercial SaaS, so move hosts to sell.

sections.label: The stack
sections.para: Static files with native components; GitHub Pages to build, another static host to sell, or the folder shipped; a passkey with PRF; browser storage, an encrypted vault or the user's Drive; the user's capped key; payment by the provider, or a link with credit kept by the user.

sections.label: How to build it
sections.line: Agents, a dev and a main site, synthetic users, and an explorer first.
sections.para: An agent session maintains the repository, with a dev site for changes and a main site for customers. Synthetic users test every release. The team is hired as explorers, villagers, then town planners, and the first hire is an explorer working with the agents.

sections.label: How to charge for it
sections.line: Charge for value: the build, the users, the keys, the installation.
sections.para: Costs are almost nothing, so price is about value: a project to build a customer's site, a price per user, a share or fee for the keys even when users bring their own, and a licence for running it inside a customer's network.

sections.label: For agents: the next steps
sections.line: Twelve steps an agent can mark done.
sections.para: From one repository with dev and main, through no backend, web components, vendoring, offline and portable hosting, passkey sign-in, storage, the user's key and a simulation mode, to synthetic users and a payment path with no server of yours.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Phase one, a proposed name, terms that change, and products that do not fit.
sections.para: Some products will need a server later. The name is a proposal. Provider terms are as of 20 October 2026. Shared state between users needs more. This is a blueprint; the MVP is next.

sections.line: A voice memo, provider documentation, coding.sgit.ai and earlier articles.
sections.para: A voice memo of 20 October 2026; provider documentation checked that day; coding.sgit.ai for components; earlier articles on passkeys, your own key, less code, Cloudflare, explorer coding, your own newsroom, paying after the value and the vault across profiles; and Wardley on pioneers, settlers and town planners.
